newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end sharply down on USDA crop report.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end sharply down on USDA crop report.

text.p: A surprise estimate by the U.S. Department of Agriculture pressured FCOJ futures the daily limit lower in most of the back months and sharply lower in spot-March, where prices remained through the close.

March closed down 5.35 cents to 74.55 cents a lb, having ranged from 74.75 to a new contract low of 72.50 cents. The back months settled the 5.00-cent daily limit to 4.20 lower, having made fresh life-of-contract lows across the board.

Players had anticipated losses to the Florida crop in the wake of the Jan 19 freeze. Instead, the USDA kept the box count unchanged at 220 million 90-lb boxes and raised yields to 1.54 gallons per box from 1.53 gallons per box.
"Growers were surprised and wondered whose oranges they (USDA) were counting," Allendale analyst Jim Cordier, said.
Analysts said the USDA probably underestimated the crop in its initial report and would have raised the box count without the freeze.

According to the USDA, "temperatures were not low enough, long enough to cause serious damage to citrus trees." Harvesting accelerated on the early fruit with most of the damaged crops going to the processors, it said.

The estimate pushed the outer months the daily 5.00-cent limit down on the open on mixed selling and a dearth of buying. March opened sharply lower but local buying kept the contract from slipping the 10.00-cent limit, traders said.
Technically, support was pegged between 67.00 and 66.00 cents a lb in March. Cordier said buying could emerge Thursday, and put support higher at 72.00 cents basis March.

But other market sources anticipate further losses. They said the estimate shows that Florida remains on track to produce a record crop. Coupled with ample supplies in Brazil and high retail prices and sluggish demand in the U.S., the report will continue to push prices to new lows.
The 1996/97 estimate of Florida temples was unchanged at 2.50 million boxes, 16 percent above last year. The Valencia forecast was cut by 3 million boxes to 87.0 million boxes.
